task: independent body-filter routing and continuity review
scope: Static review of effective filtering, live controls, reset/prepare, outgoing snapshots, idle/reuse and size/color routing; a standalone filter lifecycle probe supplements the existing engine integration evidence.
routing_review: The body receives the same effective cutoffHp/cutoffLp and modulated hpQ/lpQ computed for its rank, including filter envelopes, keyboard contour, initial/after touch, macro/global brilliance and modulation routes.

Intrinsic body brightness is supplied directly as rs.bodyBrightness; the removed LP/envelope-derived scalar does not apply a second spectral change. Pressure has a separately authored effort response as well as its explicit panel-filter route.
Resonant size is passed to InstrumentBody.noteOn once and affects authored modal/formant weights. It is not applied to live tick frequency or to the body-filter cutoff.

The body filter has its own bounded linear response: Q is clamped to 0.5..4, cutoff to 8 Hz..0.45*internalRate. This is not identical to the nonlinear circuit filter topology or its complete resonance range.

Coefficients update every 16 internal samples; the cache depends on cutoff/Q and prepare resets the stage caches after a rate change. Switch targets update each sample and crossfade with a 1 ms time constant.
Off bodies bypass body processing. With an enabled body at zero mix, internal body/filter state can advance, but both scalar and batched VCA paths exclude the body blend entirely.
lifecycle_review: prepare configures both current and previous body/filter states and recomputes the 3 ms internal-sample handoff length; hard reset and panic clear both filters and the handoff counter.

On reassignment, the outgoing filter is copied by value alongside its excitation, last pitch, color and pressure. tickFrozen retains its previous coefficients and switch targets. The incoming filter resets unconditionally.
A previous body is copied only when the voice was active and that rank has positive retained envelope value. A fully inactive voice or zero-valued rank clears the old snapshot.
When the complete voice is inactive, the idle circuit path continues before optional body/filter processing. Those filters are not ticked during the decimated silent circuit updates.

When one rank becomes silent while the other keeps its voice active, its enabled body/filter can continue ticking. Body ticking already had this lifetime before the filter revision; the new filter adds work in this case. No speculative lifetime optimization was made, and the separate runtime review measures full-engine cost.

existing_engine_evidence.coverage: Exact scalar/batched and partition agreement, full-body HP/LP/resonance and keyboard-contour routing, Off/zero-mix and source-policy isolation, next-note model selection, and released-voice handoffs at 44.1/48/96 kHz.

additional_probe.checks: Used-vs-fresh re-prepare equivalence; reset-vs-fresh equivalence; copied frozen-filter equivalence while the incoming filter is retuned; finite output under rapid endpoint/invalid cutoff and Q controls with bypass changes; exactly zero residue after reset.

limitations: The standalone filter probe does not qualify packaged hosts, real-time deadlines, arbitrary nonfinite audio inputs or perceptual quality.
The existing engine integration log is reused rather than presented as a newly executed full-engine suite.
The bound applies to the stated test signal and control schedule, not every possible musical input or automation trajectory.
